narrative.overview:
The Gambi landing reads as a particle detector's event display: one session frozen at one instant, with each person's track arriving at the hub from the outer ring. Concentric rings carry the meaning. The thick outer band is the people's machines, the dotted rings inside it are the tunnels, and the filled disc at the centre is the hub. Your app sits outside the rings and reaches them through the hub. Color is reserved for tracks and stops. Signal yellow marks a model, cyan marks an agent (a harness), and red appears only where something stays behind on its owner's machine.

Two themes share one display. Graphite is the detector hall: a near-black ground with no glow. Paper is the same display printed: a cool off-white ground with darker inks and the same roles. Code panels and the event log stay on a dark slab in both themes.

Surfaces are flat and drawn with hairlines. One variable family, Archivo, covers all reading text, and its width axis does the work a second typeface would: expanded for headlines and names, condensed for labels pinned to the display. Mono appears only for literal text a reader could type or receive. Each section is one figure with its explanation beside or under it, so density stays moderate and the figure carries the argument.
keyCharacteristics: Concentric rings and curved tracks are the drawing vocabulary for every system diagram on the page.
Yellow, cyan, and red have fixed meanings (model, agent, stop) on a neutral ink and steel base.
One variable sans whose width axis encodes role, plus mono for literal strings.
Flat surfaces, hairline borders, no shadows.
Each figure animates on one timeline and settles to a meaningful end frame.

rules.name: The Track Color Rule
rules.body: Yellow means a model and cyan means an agent, wherever they appear: tracks, dots, offers, spokes, packets. Neither color is used for decoration or emphasis unrelated to a participant.

rules.name: The Red Stops Rule
rules.body: Red marks the place where something stops: the key wedges, the wall in the section cut, what never leaves the machine, the trusted-network warning, a rejected step. Nothing else on the page is red.

rules.name: The Printed Display Rule
rules.body: Paper is the same display printed. Every role keeps its meaning across themes and only the values shift for contrast. Code panels and the event log stay dark in both themes.

rules.name: The Width Axis Rule
rules.body: Width encodes role. Condensed widths (76 to 80) are for uppercase labels and offers pinned to a figure; 100 is for anything read as prose; expanded widths (104 to 118) are for names, titles, and the wordmark.

rules.name: The Literal Mono Rule
rules.body: Mono is reserved for strings a reader could type or receive verbatim: the install command, the session code, frame and event names, endpoints, paths, and snippets. Labels that only look technical stay in Archivo.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Anything that counts or changes in place uses tabular numerals: readouts, the 1 → N switch, and model offers.

rules.name: The Zone Alignment Rule
rules.body: When a figure explains layers, each layer's text sits under the part of the drawing it explains. The section cut's columns start exactly where its zones start.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separate things with a 1px line or a tonal step. Surfaces never get drop shadows, glows, or blur.

rules.name: The Same Bend Rule
rules.body: In the ring display and the example stages, every track is one quadratic curve from the machine ring into the hub, with its control point turned the same 14° and its end turned further the same way. All tracks swirl the same way, so no two ever cross.

rules.name: The Ring Grammar Rule
rules.body: Line style names the ring: solid for machines, dotted for tunnels. Your app is never a ring; where it is drawn at all, it is a small box outside the rings. The same grammar carries into the section cut, the example stages, and the link card.

rules.name: The One Timeline Rule
rules.body: Each figure animates from one clock. The display's tracks, wedges, labels, and readouts all read one morph value; the section cut's column highlights read the packet's position; an example's tokens and log lines advance through one sequential step list. A figure never runs two independent loops.

rules.name: The Inward Outward Rule
rules.body: Tracks draw inward, from machine to hub, because the participant opens the connection. Requests travel outward, from hub to machine, because the hub dispatches into the tunnel; answers return inward.

rules.name: The End Frame Rule
rules.body: Without JS or with reduced motion, every figure shows its final, meaningful state. Animation plays into that state and never replaces it.

rules.name: The One Primary Rule
rules.body: A view has one filled primary button. Anything else beside it is a text link or the command button.

dos: **Do** draw new system diagrams from the ring vocabulary in `geometry.ts`: machines on the outside, tunnels between, the hub at the centre, and your app outside the rings.
**Do** color every track, dot, spoke, packet, and offer by what the participant brings: signal yellow for a model, cyan for an agent.
**Do** put a ground-colored halo behind any text that sits over rings or tracks (`paint-order: stroke` in SVG, `-webkit-text-stroke` with `paint-order: stroke fill` in HTML).
**Do** set uppercase labels condensed (width 76 to 80) with 0.08 to 0.09em tracking, and headlines expanded (width 108 to 118) with negative tracking.
**Do** keep one filled primary button per view and pair it with a text link or the command button.
**Do** separate content with 1px Line or Line 2 rules and tonal steps between ground, panel, and sheet.
**Do** render the end frame first, then animate into it, and pause any loop when its figure is off screen or the tab is hidden.
**Do** use tabular numerals for counts and readouts, and keep mono for literal commands, frames, events, and code.
donts: **Don't** use red for anything except a stop: keys, logins, what stays on a person's machine, the trusted-network warning, a rejected step.
**Don't** add drop shadows, glows, blur, or gradient fills to surfaces.
**Don't** let tracks in a ring figure cross or bend in different directions.
**Don't** run two independent animation clocks inside one figure.
**Don't** set labels, headings, or numbers in mono when they are not literal strings.
**Don't** put a second filled button next to the primary.
**Don't** use yellow or cyan for decoration or for emphasis unrelated to a participant.
**Don't** reintroduce a hand-painted or playful look; PRODUCT.md binds the visual to serious and direct.
